claims.text: The investigated HEA is equimolar WTaTiVZr.
The WTaTiVZr HEA has a controlled BCC microstructure.
The HEA and pure-tungsten specimens can be compared with similar initial grain sizes and identical processing conditions.
Atomic-size mismatch among W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr produces severe lattice distortion in the HEA.
The lattice distortion creates heterogeneous local stress fields.
The heterogeneous local stress fields increase dislocation cross-slip.
The heterogeneous local stress fields increase dislocation mobility at high temperature.
Increased cross-slip produces a more spatially distributed dislocation network.
The proposed dislocation behavior improves plastic-strain accommodation relative to pure tungsten.
The proposed dislocation behavior improves toughness relative to pure tungsten.
Relative to pure tungsten, the HEA will have a higher mobile-dislocation density under the specified loading.
Relative to pure tungsten, the HEA will exhibit more cross-slip events.
Relative to pure tungsten, the HEA will undergo greater plastic deformation before failure.
Relative to pure tungsten, the HEA will exhibit lower creep displacement rates under identical loading.
Pure tungsten has a more uniform lattice than the WTaTiVZr HEA.
Pure tungsten's more uniform lattice limits dislocation cross-slip and redistribution.
The proposed mechanism applies at 700–900°C under high static and cyclic stresses relevant to plasma-facing-component service.
The proposed mechanism may not apply at lower temperatures or under deformation modes unlike plasma-facing service.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis associates lattice distortion with increased dislocation mobility yet predicts reduced creep, while assigning pure tungsten both more restricted dislocation motion and greater creep. The fields do not distinguish plastic glide/cross-slip mobility from the rate-controlling mobility or diffusion processes governing creep, leaving an unresolved causal tension.
